note: Qualified capability records, not a support matrix and not the backlog. A record exists only for behaviour that has been exercised. 'identify-only' means structural recognition without decoding. Every operation reflects what the implementation actually claims, and the accompanying tests assert that each named entry point exists.

status_meanings.qualified: Exercised against synthetic or hand-authored specimens with independent cross-checking where an independent implementation exists.
status_meanings.partial: Supported only for a named subset of the format's variants; other variants are reported unsupported rather than decoded.
status_meanings.identify-only: Recognised structurally; contents are not decoded.
status_meanings.unsupported: Deliberately reported unsupported, with the reason recorded.
status_meanings.planned: No implementation. Listed so the gap is explicit rather than implied.
status_meanings.blocked: Implementation is prevented by a missing specification or specimen.

formats.title: ZIP archive
formats.evidence: Portable tests cover stored and deflated members, unsafe paths, symbolic links, byte budgets, member-count limits and a malformed central directory.

identification.structural: PK signature with a central directory at the end of file
unsupported_variants: Methods other than store and deflate need the optional 7-Zip adapter.

formats.limitations: Shrink and Implode members require the optional 7-Zip adapter and are verified against the central-directory size and CRC. Encrypted and non-regular members are reported, never written.

formats.title: POSIX tar archive
formats.evidence: Portable tests cover a nested gzip/tar pair plus a symbolic-link member.

identification.structural: ustar magic at offset 257 within the first header block

formats.limitations: Sparse members and non-regular types are reported as such. Header checksums are read by the standard library but not independently validated here.

formats.title: gzip stream (.gz, .tgz)
formats.evidence: Portable test decompresses a synthetic tar.gz and identifies the inner ustar archive by structure.

identification.structural: 1F 8B 08 header with a deflate body

formats.limitations: One member only, named from the containing filename. Multi-member streams are not enumerated.

formats.title: ARC (SEA ARC) archive
formats.evidence: Stored members, methods 8 and 9 are decoded natively and checked against the stored member CRC. The method-8 rules were resolved on 2026-11-26 from nomarch 1.4's published decoder and then confirmed on genuine material: all four method-8 members of the two TVDog archives (6195, 726, 5366 and 128 unpacked bytes) reproduce their stored CRC and consume their packed bytes exactly, so both archives now extract completely, five members of five. ARC wrote its codes in padded groups of eight and padded a group before a width change, and code 256 only returns the width to nine bits without clearing the string table. A synthetic encoder in the portable suite covers literal runs, RLE90 escapes, width growth, table saturation and the 256 shrink; 7-Zip 26.05 has no ARC handler, so nomarch remained a comparison rather than a required backend.

identification.structural: member header followed by a 1A 00 end-of-archive marker
unsupported_variants: Methods 3 to 7 are reported unsupported; methods 5 and 6 can be routed through an optional nomarch build.
Method 9 is decoded natively but has synthetic coverage only, with no genuine specimen yet.

formats.limitations: Methods 3 to 7 are reported unsupported; methods 5 and 6 use a hashed 12-bit table that has not been studied, and are only reachable through an optional nomarch build. Method 9 shares the method-8 code path but has not been seen in a genuine archive. The 16-bit CRC covers the unpacked member only, and a CRC mismatch is reported as a read error rather than as its own status.

formats.title: LHA / LZH level-0 archive
formats.evidence: Portable test builds level-0 members by hand and checks the header checksum, the CRC-16 and the binary-stdout adapter contract.

identification.structural: '-lh' or '-lz' header level with a leading length byte
unsupported_variants: Compressed LZ methods need the optional 7-Zip adapter.

formats.limitations: Only level-0 headers are parsed natively. Availability of an external helper is a deployment property, not a code property.

formats.title: ARJ, CAB, RAR, 7z and ISO/UDF listing through 7-Zip
formats.evidence: Portable tests drive the adapter with synthetic list output, including link entries, ambiguous names and a non-archive executable listing.

identification.structural: no signature of its own; delegated to an external lister
unsupported_variants: Nothing is decoded without the external adapter.

formats.limitations: Nothing here is an independent implementation of these formats; the adapter is bounded by member count, output bytes, a deadline and a single stdout stream. 7-Zip availability and version must be recorded per run.

formats.title: Unix compress(1) LZW stream (.Z)
formats.evidence: Portable tests generate streams at every maximum code width from 9 to 16 that cross one or more width transitions, in block and non-block mode, with a dictated dictionary CLEAR and with the table saturated. gzip 1.15's independent unlzw decoder reproduced every payload from the 10-16 bit streams byte for byte, which validates the generator's eight-code group convention rather than our decoder's assumptions; our decoder then reproduced the same bytes and the same termination. The earlier direction still holds: 7-Zip 26.05 extracted this project's encoded streams byte-identically.

identification.structural: 1F 9D header carrying maxbits and a block flag
unsupported_variants: The stream records no length or checksum, so output cannot be verified.

formats.limitations: Codes are packed in groups of eight; a width change and a block-mode CLEAR both pad the current group at the old width, and the group origin is re-based after every jump. A CLEAR resumes without resetting the previous code, exactly as ncompress's decoder does, and a full table freezes rather than widening past maxbits. A stream that ends inside a code is reported as partial with truncated-final-code instead of as a complete member. Output bytes, code count and decoder working memory are bounded separately; the decoder's tables are fixed by maxbits and do not follow output. Nine-bit streams are decoded but not cross-validated, because gzip 1.15 rejects one once its table fills; the difference is recorded rather than smoothed over. Reserved header bits 0x20 and 0x40 are reported as reserved-header-flags. No encoder is shipped.

formats.title: bzip2 stream (.bz2)
formats.evidence: Round-trip, truncation, corruption, trailing-data, concatenated-stream and output-bound cases are covered by portable tests. Every member's declared block size is checked against the caller's decoder-memory bound before that member's decoder is constructed, so a small first member cannot authorise a larger later one, and a later member that declares 900 kB blocks is refused under a 1 MiB budget. The number of concatenated streams is bounded separately from the output budget, and a damaged later member keeps the members that already verified their CRC as partial output.

identification.structural: 'BZh' block magic followed by a level digit

formats.limitations: Decoding uses the CPython standard library; the independent-implementation claim rests on CPython, not on this project. bzip2 keeps several block-sized tables whose size the stream header declares, so decoder memory is bounded through that declaration rather than by the output budget. The comparison uses bzip2(1)'s documented decompression requirement per block size (500 KiB at 100 kB rising to 3700 KiB at 900 kB), which covers libbzip2's tt allocation and its fixed tables; four block bytes would understate it. decoder_bytes is a per-decoder peak: members are decoded one at a time and the previous decompressor is released before the next is constructed, so the budget is the largest member's requirement, not the sum. The figures are the vendor's documented estimates, not measured on this machine, and the standard library never selects the 2.5-bytes-per-block-byte -s decoder.

formats.title: xz stream (.xz)
formats.evidence: Round-trip, concatenated-stream, trailing-data, truncation, integrity and output-bound cases are exercised by portable tests, and a block declaring a 16 MiB dictionary is refused under a 64 KiB decoder-memory bound. A later member of a concatenated file is decoded by its own LZMADecompressor with the same memlimit, so it cannot raise the budget either.

identification.structural: FD 37 7A 58 5A 00 stream header

formats.limitations: Decoding uses the CPython standard library with memlimit taken from the decoder-memory bound, because a small stream can declare a large dictionary and allocate it before emitting a byte. Every member of a concatenated file gets its own decoder with that same memlimit, and only one decoder is live at a time, so the stream count and the working-memory bound are enforced per member. Legacy .lzma alone streams are not handled by this record.

formats.title: ImageDisk sector image (.imd)
formats.evidence: Hand-authored fixtures exercise raw, fill-byte, absent, deleted-data-address-mark and read-error sector statuses; a normalised image is then handed to the FAT12 reader end to end. Three genuine ImageDisk images then qualified the reader against real media: two complete 400-sector hard-disk images normalise with no gaps, and a 40-cylinder diagnostic disk parses 440 sector records with zero unknown statuses while exercising both the raw and fill paths. Sector placement is confirmed by content, since a normalised image begins with a Z80 boot jump.

identification.structural: 'IMD <version>:' identifying line before the 1A comment terminator
unsupported_variants: Track modes outside raw, RLE and fill are reported unsupported.

formats.limitations: Per-sector cylinder and head maps and a 0xFF per-sector size table are parsed. The diagnostic specimen repeats one sector ID on its head-1 tracks, which is preserved as 40 reported conflicts rather than silently resolved. Physical recording attributes (data rate, encoding) are recorded from the track mode and not verified against media. Decoding enforces the caller's input-byte, per-sector, aggregate-decoded, per-track sector and geometry bounds before it allocates, so a declared track length or sector count cannot enlarge them.

formats.title: Sydex TeleDisk image (.td0), ordinary compression
formats.evidence: Hand-authored fixtures exercise raw, repeated-2-byte-pattern and RLE sector methods, the skipped (0x10) and ID-only (0x20) flags, comments and truncation. Three genuine images then qualified the header: the CRC-16 polynomial 0xA097 with preset 0 over the first ten bytes reproduces all three stored values (0x0A52, 0x609C, 0x17FB), which no competing convention does. The same specimens disproved a signature check byte: byte 3 is a volume-set identifier reading 0x42, 0x43 and 0x2E, so identification now uses the version byte and the header CRC, and all three files are recognised. The two ordinary images parse to 800 and 640 sectors with no unknown status. Both block conventions are confirmed by the same data: 359 RLE and 426 repeat-pattern sectors decode to exactly their declared size, and the first RLE block of one image is a literal block that expands to the DOS 2.11 boot record (E9 83 00, "ZDS 2.0") and normalises to a complete 640-sector volume.
formats.limitations: The 'td' advanced variant compresses the whole post-header stream with an LZSS/Huffman coder; it is recognised, its header metadata is reported, and its payload is deliberately not decoded. Sector payloads carry no checksum, so completeness is structural rather than verified; exact decoded length is necessary rather than sufficient evidence for the block conventions, so a coincidence on real but repetitive disk data is not excluded. One genuine CP/M-86 image declares 800 sectors that collapse onto 400 logical sectors, and the normaliser reports the 400 unwritten sectors rather than inventing a head mapping. Decoding enforces the caller's input-byte, per-sector, aggregate-decoded and per-track sector bounds before allocating, and the normaliser refuses a geometry or logical-image size outside its own bounds instead of allocating it.

identification.structural: TD or td signature with a plausible version byte and a verified header CRC-16
unsupported_variants: The 'td' advanced variant compresses its payload with LZSS/Huffman and is not decoded.

formats.title: Sydex CopyQM image (.qm, .cqm)

specifications.title: LibDsk appendix M: the CopyQM file format

formats.evidence: Hand-authored fixtures check the zero-byte-sum header invariant, the embedded BPB geometry, signed run lengths, a leading comment block, a truncated track and an implausible cylinder count. One fixture is a FAT12 volume extracted end to end.

identification.structural: 'CQ 14' signature with a zero-byte-sum header
unsupported_variants: The 32-bit disk-data CRC is recorded but not verified.

formats.limitations: The documented disk-data CRC (32-bit, top two bits excluded) is recorded but not verified. Payload runs are decoded per track; a damaged run keeps every complete sector it described and names the remainder missing. A track is expanded only after its declared sectors-per-track, track length and total geometry are checked against the caller's track, sector, aggregate-byte and geometry budgets, and the sector cap is applied to the whole track before the inner sector loop can run.

formats.title: Disk Copy Fast image (.dcf)
formats.evidence: No structural test exists, because no specification does.

identification.structural: no published byte-level specification
unsupported_variants: No published specification, so neither identification nor extraction is claimed.

formats.limitations: Blocked: no published byte-level specification was found for Disk Copy Fast, and its distribution carries no format description. Contemporary sources agree only that it holds a raw floppy image with a leading header. Implementing it from file size or extension would be guessing; it needs a real specimen plus controlled reverse engineering. Aaru's 'CisCopy .DCF' is a different program and must not be used as a substitute.

formats.title: FAT12 and FAT16 filesystem
formats.evidence: Portable tests read a synthetic FAT12 volume, follow a directory chain, and reject a self-referencing cluster chain. Container tests reach the same reader through a normalised IMD and CopyQM image.

identification.structural: BPB geometry with a 12- or 16-bit allocation table
unsupported_variants: Only 8.3 short names here: long names belong to the FAT32/VFAT record.

formats.limitations: Eight-bit short names are the primary view; long names and the FAT32 cluster threshold belong to the FAT32/VFAT record, which shares this reader. Cluster chains are validated for loops, truncation and bad-cluster markers, so a corrupt extent is reported rather than padded. Twelve-bit chains are exercised directly: portable tests build a two-cluster FAT12 extent, a bad-cluster marker and a self-referencing chain on a volume whose fixed root region is read in place. Cluster ownership is recorded per directory entry, so a file aliasing another entry's clusters is refused while the first keeps its bytes.

formats.title: ISO 9660 with 2048-byte logical blocks
formats.evidence: Recognition checks the primary volume descriptor, mirrored volume sizes and the logical block length; four real images from the project mirror were listed. See docs/ecosystem/tvdog-extraction-capabilities.json.

identification.structural: 'CD001' volume descriptor at sector 16

formats.limitations: Recognition and metadata are native; enumeration and extraction are delegated to 7-Zip. No completeness claim for multisession media or every extension record.

formats.title: UDF on cooked media
formats.evidence: Recognition by NSR02/NSR03 anchor descriptor; one independently generated bridge image was listed and one member extracted.

identification.structural: NSR02 or NSR03 descriptor sequence

formats.limitations: No UDF-only extraction qualification. A hybrid disc is currently identified as ISO because the primary descriptor is checked first.

formats.title: 2352-byte raw Mode 1 / Mode 2 Form 1 sector candidate
formats.evidence: Synthetic raw Mode 1 descriptor only.

identification.structural: 2352-byte raw sector framing with a mode byte at offset 15

formats.limitations: Structural recognition alone: no raw-track decoding, CUE pairing or per-sector integrity verification.

formats.title: PDF text extraction
formats.evidence: The worker protocol is tested with synthetic page rows, including a page-level error and an empty-text page that is triaged for OCR.

identification.structural: '%PDF-' header
unsupported_variants: Text extraction only; no rendering or object-level validation.

formats.limitations: Text only. Pages are preserved with one-based numbering; an image-only scan needs a separate OCR pass.

formats.evidence: Portable tests confirm an unrecognised executable stays 'unhandled' while a self-extracting payload is listed.

identification.structural: 'MZ' header, PE when e_lfanew reaches 'PE\0\0'
unsupported_variants: Self-extracting payloads are listed through the optional adapter and never executed.

formats.evidence: Not implemented.

formats.title: FAT32 and VFAT long file names
formats.evidence: Portable tests build sparse volumes whose cluster count sits above the FAT32 threshold, so the 32-bit allocation table, the cluster-chained root directory and the high cluster-word merge are all exercised: a file placed at cluster 0x10003 is read back byte for byte. A three-slot VFAT long name with non-ASCII characters is reconstructed instead of its 8.3 alias, and a chain whose checksum does not cover the short name falls back to that alias. Damaged structures are exercised separately: a bad-cluster marker ends the read with an error rather than passing for an end of chain, a self-referencing chain is rejected, a cross-linked second file is refused while the first keeps its bytes, a declared length beyond the chain is an error, and a volume too short for its declared total is not read as a filesystem. BPB_ExtFlags selects the active allocation-table copy, divergent mirrored copies are reported as fat-copy-N-differs, and FSInfo and backup boot sectors are checked and reported as observations rather than trusted. Every VFAT slot is now validated individually: the reserved order bit, the reserved byte and zero first-cluster field, the checksum each slot repeats, strict descending ordinals with a unique 0x40 marker, contiguous slots 1..N, UTF-16 legality including surrogate pairing and FFFF padding after the terminator, and the short entry immediately following. A stale chain followed by a valid one no longer shadows it, and a malformed chain falls back to the short name with a named observation. Ownership is recorded per directory entry rather than per name, so duplicate names stay distinct objects and a file aliasing a directory chain, the FAT32 root chain or another entry is refused; directory chains are claimed before they are walked.
formats.limitations: Only contiguous descending long-name chains bound to a matching short-name checksum are accepted; anything else leaves the short name plus a named observation. Observations are split into damage and advice: a divergent mirrored FAT, an invalid FSInfo signature, or a backup boot sector that differs or sits outside the reserved region is damage and makes the listing partial, while an implausible free-cluster hint is advice only. FSInfo values and the backup boot sector are never used to allocate or place files. Directory chains are claimed and cross-link checked, including the FAT32 root. No volume created by an independent filesystem implementation has been qualified yet: the fixtures are written from the on-disk structures, so these tests qualify the reader against the specification rather than against dosfstools or Windows.

identification.structural: BPB whose cluster count reaches the FAT32 threshold, with a cluster-based root directory
unsupported_variants: A long name whose checksum does not cover its short name falls back to the short name.
Volume-level inconsistencies such as divergent mirrored allocation tables or an invalid FSInfo signature are reported as observations, not repaired.

unsupported_variants: Not implemented: the layout belongs to the geometry layer.
